texts: I used to read about longing for years, but only when I waited for someone myself, restless as a moth and thirsting like a rainbird, did I truly know it.
Give me a doha saying that the moth knows the burn and the rainbird knows the thirst only because they lived it, so only what I have seen and felt myself can be called known.
moth, rainbird, own eyes
The moth knows the burning, the rainbird the thirst; no one told them, they lived it, and that alone is knowing.
doha: moth n rainbird know it bc they lived it, not read it
My grandfather never trusted talk; he would watch a bee work and sift grain in a winnowing fan himself before saying he understood anything.
I'd like a doha about trusting only what I have watched with my own eyes, like a bee that tastes each blossom itself and a farmer who sifts with his own winnowing fan, not repeating others.
doha w bee + winnowing fan: believe only what u saw urself
bee, winnowing fan, seen myself
The bee tastes before it sings; the winnowing fan shows the grain; what my own eyes have seen I call true.
doha: i dont believe the moneylender's words, only what i saw myself
moneylender, seen myself
Write a doha about a man who heard endless tales of the moneylender's cruelty but believed none until he stood in the line himself and saw it with his own eyes.
Everyone warned me about the local moneylender, but I only understood after I went to him myself and saw how he treated people.
Rumors of the moneylender drifted like smoke; only when I stood before him did I know what he was.
doha about trusting what u saw w ur own eyes not what u heard
What the ear gathers is borrowed, what the eye has seen is mine; I believe only the latter.
Craft a doha saying that I will not repeat what I have only read or been told, because real knowing comes only from walking through a thing myself and seeing it with my own eyes.
seen, not heard
My friends all told me the city was awful, but after I lived there a year I saw for myself it was not like that at all.
Read a hundred sayings about the seed, yet only the one you sow yourself will teach you.
I read many gardening articles but never understood anything until I put my own hands in the soil and watched a seed sprout.
seed, sowing myself
Please make a doha about someone who learned nothing from descriptions of how a seed becomes a plant until he planted one himself and watched, day after day, with his own eyes.
doha: u only get it when u plant the seed urself
ash, one-string lute, lived
A wandering singer with a one-string lute once told me that he trusted no teaching until he had sat by the ash of his own grief and understood it himself.
doha w ash n one-string lute: only what i lived is real knowing
The one-string lute sings what the singer lived; the ash tells what he has burned; borrowed songs have no truth.
Write a doha about a singer with a one-string lute who sits in the ash of his own sorrow and sings only what he has lived through, trusting no knowledge that did not come from his own life.
Please write a doha for someone who is tired of advice and opinions, saying that the only knowing worth having is what one has seen and lived through personally, not what one has read or been told.
doha on learning by doing, not by hearing
Everyone gave me advice on running a business, and none of it helped until I made the mistakes myself and finally understood.
knowing by living
Not by hearsay, not by page, but by walking the road myself have I come to know.
For years I was told the old trunk's lock was stuck for good, and only when I lit a lamp and tried it myself did I find the trick; I believe my own hands now.
I need a doha about a man who trusted no one's word that the lock could not be opened, and by lamplight tried it himself, learning with his own hands what no description could have taught.
By the lamp's small light I tried the lock myself, and what I touched became what I know.
lamp, lock, tried myself
doha w lamp n lock: i believe only what i tried myself
date palm, seen myself
Can you put together a doha about a man who heard that the date palm gives sweet fruit only far above, and who climbed it himself, tasting and knowing what no description could have told him.
I had heard how hard it was to climb a date palm, but I only understood when I did it myself, scraping my arms and tasting the fruit.
doha: date palm fruit tastes different when u climb it urself
I did not trust the tales of the date palm; I climbed, and the sweetness at the top was mine.
A priest in our area counts his prayer beads and recites what he has read, but my old neighbor simply says what he has seen with his own eyes, and I trust him more.
priest, prayer beads, seen
doha: priest tells what he read w his prayer beads, i trust only what i saw
The priest turns his prayer beads and repeats the words of others; I speak only of what these eyes have seen.
Write a doha about a priest who counts prayer beads and recites what was handed to him, while a simple man speaks only of what he has seen and lived, and so knows more.
I read many descriptions of thirst, but only when I walked a whole day and then lifted a pot of water to my lips did I truly know it.
Give me a doha showing that no description of thirst can match the moment one drinks from a pot of water after a long walk, because what is lived is known and what is told is only a word.
Say what you will of thirst; the pot of water in a parched hand teaches more than any telling.
pot of water, felt myself
doha: pot of water tastes best when ur actually thirsty, u gotta live it
furnace, palanquin, lived
The furnace teaches what no tale can; the palanquin's rider knows nothing of those who bear it.
I'd like a doha about a man who rode in a palanquin and never knew the heat of the furnace, until he worked a day beside it and learned with his own body what all the stories could not teach.
I grew up being carried everywhere in comfort, like a palanquin rider, and only after I worked a day at a furnace did I know what labor truly is.
doha: palanquin ride vs furnace work, u dont know til u live it
I had seen pictures of the ocean my whole life, but when I finally stood on the shore and felt the spray, I knew that all the pictures had said nothing.
A thousand tellings of the ocean are a drop; one look from the shore is the whole of it.
Compose a doha saying that no one can describe the ocean to a person who has never seen it, because what the eyes have beheld and the body felt is knowledge no words can lend.
ocean, seen myself
doha: u cant know the ocean from stories, u gotta go see it
The needle pricks, the sandalwood cools; I know them not from sayings but from the touch of my own skin.
I read a lot about herbal remedies, yet I only understood sandalwood paste when I applied it on a burn myself, and a pricked finger taught me what the needle does.
doha w sandalwood n needle: touch it urself to know
sandalwood, needle, touched
Craft a doha about learning the coolness of sandalwood and the sting of a needle not from books or tales but by touching them with my own hand and feeling them with my own skin.
doha: u dont know salt til u taste it urself
My mother always said that salt can't be explained, you have to taste it, and I realized as an adult that all real knowing is like that.
salt, tasted myself
Please make a doha showing that a thousand descriptions of salt's flavor are nothing beside one taste, so that what I have tasted and lived myself is known and the rest is only heard.
Describe the salt as you will; one grain upon the lips tells it all.
doha w leaf + tortoise: watching it myself taught me more than reading
I watched the tortoise nibble a leaf, slowly, and learned more than a hundred sayings could say.
Write a doha about a person who spent a whole day watching a tortoise eat a leaf, and learned patience from it with his own eyes, which no lesson he had read or heard had ever taught.
leaf, tortoise, watched myself
I read about patience for years, but only when I watched a tortoise cross my garden and reach a leaf did I truly see what it means.
At dawn I stood in the dew and watched a swan glide past, and in that moment I understood what the elders meant about calm, which no one's words had made me feel.
I need a doha about someone who watched a swan on the morning dew and understood stillness with his own eyes, which the sayings and sermons had never been able to give him.
Dew on the morning grass, a swan in the silence; what I saw with my eyes is what I know.
doha w dew n swan: i saw it myself that morning
dew, swan, seen
I have read the maps and heard the tales; only the road beneath my own feet has taught me anything.
doha on knowing things only after u live them
Can you put together a doha for a young man who collects opinions about life from everyone, telling him that one day of living a thing teaches more than a hundred days of hearing about it.
lived, not told
I used to give confident advice about grief, until it happened to me, and then I knew I had known nothing.
Before I became a parent I thought I understood all about it from friends and articles, but the first night alone with my baby showed me I had understood nothing.
doha abt knowing from living, not from what ppl say
The heard and the read are shallow water; only the lived is deep.
Compose a doha that says what I have seen with my own eyes, tasted and endured, I call knowledge, and what I have only been told I hold lightly, however grand the teller.
seen with own eyes
My daughter doesn't believe anything till she has tried it herself, and honestly I admire it; I'd like a doha on that stubborn way of knowing.
Please write a doha about the difference between hearing about a thing and living it, saying that the person who walked through it knows what no teller, however learned, can ever convey.
short doha on seeing it urself
first-hand knowing
I did not believe the word until the thing itself stood before me.
palanquin, lived it
Carried in a palanquin, one hears of the road; walking the road, one knows it.
Give me a doha about a rich man who rode in a palanquin and thought he knew the road from others' tales, until he walked it himself and found it nothing like what he had heard.
I was always driven everywhere, and when I finally walked my city's lanes on foot, like stepping out of a palanquin, I learned how little I had seen before.
doha: palanquin ppl dont know the road, walk it urself
I'd like a doha about the rainbird that cries for a single drop and knows its own thirst better than any scholar describing thirst, because only what is felt in one's own body is truly known.
doha w a rainbird: it knows thirst bc it lives it
After a long drought on our farm I finally understood the rainbird's cry in my own throat, which no book or story could have taught me.
rainbird, felt myself
The rainbird cries not from hearing but from lived thirst; so my knowing is what I have endured.
Write a doha about a person who turned the grindstone with his own hands and watched the chakor bird at dusk himself, learning from his own seeing and labor what no teacher's account had ever shown.
grindstone, chakor bird, felt
The grindstone's weight in my hands, the chakor bird in my eyes; these are my teachers, and no others.
I had only heard about village life until I spent a month turning the grindstone and watching a chakor bird each evening, and then I truly knew.
doha w grindstone + chakor bird: what i did n saw myself
doha w palanquin n rope: u gotta carry it urself to know
palanquin, rope, carried
I only knew the weight of a palanquin after I took hold of the rope and carried one myself at a wedding, though I had watched them for years.
Craft a doha about a man who had watched palanquin-bearers all his life but understood nothing until he gripped the rope and bore the weight himself, learning it in his own shoulders.
I watched the bearers, I heard their song; only when the rope bit my own hand did I know.
I'd like a doha for those who quote others endlessly, saying that the one who has seen a thing with his own eyes needs no quotation, and that what is lived outweighs what is heard.
own eyes, own proof
My mentor never said anything she had not tried herself, and her few words carried more weight than anyone's lectures.
Let the learned argue; I have seen, and seeing is the end of arguing.
doha about trusting my own eyes
What is told fades with the telling; what is lived stays in the blood.
seeing is knowing
Please make a doha showing that the person who has met a thing face to face and endured it needs no one to certify the knowledge, since it is written in his own life.
doha on learning from my own life, not from others
When I lost my job I finally understood what everyone had been telling me about uncertainty for years.
Write a doha showing that life itself is both touchstone and furnace, testing a person as no teaching can, so that only what he has been tested through and seen with his own eyes can be called known.
touchstone, furnace, tested myself
Everyone told me I was brave, but only when life became a furnace and a touchstone did I find out what I actually knew about myself.
Not by sayings but by the furnace, not by praise but by the touchstone, did I learn what I am.
doha w touchstone n furnace: ur tested by life, not by words
bitter gourd, inn, tasted
At the inn they praised the bitter gourd; I tasted it and knew its bitterness not by hearsay but on my own palate.
doha w bitter gourd + inn: i tried it myself at the inn
At a roadside inn a stranger swore the bitter gourd curry was delicious, but only when I tasted it did I form my own opinion.
I need a doha about a person at an inn who heard many opinions about a bitter gourd dish but trusted none until he tasted it himself and knew with his own mouth.
doha: beggar at the door told me real stuff i never read

Can you put together a doha about a beggar sitting at the door who spoke only of what he had suffered and seen with his own eyes, and whose few words taught more than all the learned men's long speeches.
At the door the beggar spoke only of what he had lived, and the whole gathering fell silent to hear.
A beggar at my door once told me about hunger, and nothing I had read made me understand it as his plain words did.
door, beggar, lived
seen it myself
doha pls: trust urself, not hearsay
Write a doha reminding a young scholar that knowing a thing by living it, with his own eyes and hands, is deeper than reciting what a hundred teachers have claimed about it.
Heard, it is a rumor; read, it is a rumor too; lived, it becomes my own.
My cousin told me that moving abroad was easy, and I believed him, but it took living there myself to see how wrong that was.
tested, not told
I stopped taking people's word about cities and jobs and began going and seeing for myself, and my whole view of life has changed.
Please give me a doha that says a person should believe only what his own eyes have seen and his own life has tested, for borrowed certainty collapses when the real thing arrives.
doha: dont just believe it, go see it urself
Borrowed certainty breaks like glass; the knowing that I lived has no seams.
Give me a doha about a moth that knows the burn from its own flight, and a man who counts prayer beads and recites others' words, showing that only what is lived yields real knowing.
moth, prayer beads, lived
The moth flies into the burn and knows; the prayer beads turn in a hand that has not flown.
doha w moth + prayer beads: u gotta jump into it urself
My uncle has counted his prayer beads for forty years, repeating what he was taught, but my friend who flew into hardship like a moth knows far more.
I read every medical article about my illness, but only when a physician sat with me and I lived through the treatment did I truly understand what I had.

I'd like a doha showing that a physician who has been sick himself understands the sickness better than one who learned it only from texts, because what is lived is known and what is read is only repeated.
doha: the physician who suffered knows more than the one who read
physician, felt illness
The physician who has felt the fever knows what no manual could say.
Write a doha about a man who spent his whole life riding in a palanquin, hearing of the world from others, and who finally stepped out to see with his own eyes how different it was.
doha: palanquin guy finally walks n sees the real world
Stepping from the palanquin, he saw what a lifetime of hearing had hidden.
My grandmother was carried everywhere in comfort as a girl and often says she only learned what life was once she walked out on her own.
palanquin, seen myself
Craft a doha about a woman who churns the curd with her own hands every morning and knows the butter coming not from sayings but from the rhythm in her arms, learning by doing.
doha w churn: u know butter only when u churn it urself
The churn turns and the butter gathers; it is the arm, not the telling, that knows.
churn, did it myself
My grandmother let me use the churn one morning, and I understood in my own arms what she had been trying to tell me for years.
Everyone said that working at the furnace was hard, but I only knew after I walked in through the door one morning and stayed a whole shift.
doha w door + furnace: i walked in n saw it myself
door, furnace, entered myself
I opened the door to the furnace's roar, and what I saw there was worth more than a library of tales.
Please make a doha about a person who heard endless stories of the furnace's heat but only knew it after he entered through the door himself, feeling the heat on his own face.
The furnace's heat is not in words; stand beside it, and your skin will say what no one else could.
Write a doha showing that those who talk of the furnace's heat have not stood in front of it, while the man who has felt it on his face speaks little and knows everything.
furnace, felt myself
A blacksmith friend barely says a word about his work, yet I trust him more than the experts, because he has lived beside the furnace for decades.
doha: furnace talk vs actually standing at the furnace
Turn over a single leaf with your own hand and learn what a thousand lectures on the garden never said.
I need a doha about a person who studied plants in lectures for years but learned truly only when he held a single leaf in his hand and watched it with his own eyes through the seasons.
leaf, held myself
doha w leaf: held it in my hand, now i know
I could recite the names of every plant from class, but only when I held a leaf in my hand and studied it did I really see it.
winnowing fan, potter and clay

Can you put together a doha showing that a person who has winnowed with a fan and shaped clay with a potter's hands knows labor from within, and needs no sermon to tell him what his own hands have taught.
I spent a summer with a potter shaping clay and winnowing grain with a fan, and I learned things about patience that no teacher could have conveyed.
The fan sorts the grain, the potter shapes the clay; hands that have worked, not mouths that have talked, know.
doha w winnowing fan + potter and clay: doing it myself taught me
doha w fish n mosque: i learned by seeing, not just hearing sermons
I sat at the mosque listening to sermons for years, but one morning I watched a fish in a pond and understood something no sermon had told me.
The fish needs no sermon to know its pond; I too know only what I have seen.
Write a doha about a man who heard endless sermons at the mosque but felt true understanding only when he watched a fish swim and saw with his own eyes what the sermons had spoken of.
fish, mosque, seen
I saw it
Give me a doha saying that the word of the learned and the rumor of the crowd are both only echoes, while a single sight with my own eyes is the real sound of knowing.
doha on trusting what i saw not what i heard
Echoes are not voices; the seen is the voice.
Everyone online had a strong opinion about that place, but visiting it myself changed everything I thought.
The needle teaches by pricking, not by telling; I know it by the mark on my own finger.
doha w needle: u learn by getting pricked urself
needle, felt myself
I'd like a doha about someone who was warned many times about the needle's prick but only understood the lesson when it pierced his own finger, learning by pain what words could not teach.
People kept warning me about mending things myself, but only after a needle went into my finger did I really learn to be careful.
own eyes, own truth
doha: believe it only when u see it urself
My uncle thinks every rumor is gospel, while I only trust what I have been through, and we argue about it constantly.
I drank from my own cup, not from tales, and so I know the taste.
Write a doha showing that the person who has lived through a thing and seen it with his own eyes carries a knowing that is deeper than any fine words, and no argument can shake it.
learned by living
Craft a doha that says words may be borrowed and wisdom may be quoted, but only what I have lived through becomes my own, and no one can take it from me or give it to me.
short doha on first-hand knowing
Only after I raised children of my own did I understand what my mother went through, though I had heard her stories a hundred times.
The heard is a guest, the lived is the dweller; only the latter stays.
Please make a doha about a diver who risked his life to bring up a pearl and who understands its worth through his own breath and effort, as no buyer who only looks at it ever could.
My uncle spent years diving for pearls and always says that no one understands their worth who has not held their breath for one.
doha: pearl diver knows pearls bc he dove for them
The pearl is known to the one who dived for it, not to the one who merely admires its glow.
pearl, lived it
Write a doha about a farmer who knows the thorn's prick and the winnowing fan's rhythm through his own work, while city scholars who write about both know them only by repeating what others said.
A farmer I met spoke about thorns and winnowing with such quiet certainty that I knew he had lived it, unlike anyone I had read.
winnowing fan, thorn, lived
doha w winnowing fan + thorn: farmers know it bc they do it
The thorn has pricked his hand, the fan has sifted his grain; he speaks only of what he knows.
A skilled lock-maker at my town's furnace told me that nothing he knows came from a book, only from burned fingers and long hours of working.
I need a doha about a craftsman who forges locks at his furnace and knows each one by his own hands and the heat on his face, trusting nothing that he has not shaped himself.
lock, furnace, made myself
The furnace taught the hand, the hand taught the lock; no sermon was ever needed.
doha w lock n furnace: craftsman knows by doing
mosque, seen myself
I visited the mosque in my neighborhood after years of hearing rumors about it, and the reality was so different from what I had been told.
doha: i went to the mosque n saw it myself, not like they said

Can you put together a doha about a man who heard all kinds of claims about what happens at the mosque and decided to go and see with his own eyes, finding the reality very different from the stories.
Rumors raged about the mosque until I walked in myself; what my eyes saw silenced every tale.
doha: u dont know a thief til u meet one urself
I heard about the thief a thousand times; when he stood before me I learned who he was.
Everyone in town talked about the local thief, and it was only after I spoke with him myself that I understood him.
Write a doha about a man who had heard countless stories about a thief but knew nothing until he met him face to face and saw with his own eyes what kind of man he really was.
thief, met myself
The musk deer searches far and wide for the scent in its own navel; so too the palace-dweller seeks knowing everywhere but in what he has lived.

Give me a doha about a musk deer that searches far and wide for a fragrance it carries inside, and a king in his palace who seeks knowing in others' words, when only his own life could have taught him.
doha w musk deer + palace: knowing is what u lived, not heard
I grew up in a palace-like mansion hearing about the world from tutors, and only when I left it did I realize, like a musk deer seeking its own scent, that my knowing had to come from my own steps.
musk deer, palace, lived
